question: Under the PC and PNDT Act 1994 (as amended 2003), which of the following is a mandatory requirement before any covered prenatal diagnostic procedure is performed?

answers.text: Written consent of the husband or head of household

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: There is no requirement for husband's or household head's consent under the PCPNDT Act. The Act requires the woman's own written consent and Form F completion.

answers.text: Completion of Form F by the referring doctor and the pregnant woman, before the procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Form F (consent and declaration form) must be completed and signed by both the pregnant woman and the registered practitioner before any covered prenatal diagnostic technique. It must be preserved for 2 years.
Prior District Magistrate approval is not required. The Appropriate Authority (typically the District Health Officer) oversees compliance but does not pre-approve individual procedures.

answers.text: Certification by a genetic counsellor confirming indication

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Genetic counsellor certification is not a statutory requirement under the PCPNDT Act. The registered medical practitioner performing the procedure is responsible for verifying the indication.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the PCPNDT Act compliance requirements. Form F (pre-procedure declaration and consent form) signed by both the pregnant woman and the clinician is mandatory before any covered prenatal diagnostic technique.
Well done. Form F is the cornerstone compliance document under the PCPNDT Act — the woman's written declaration of the medical indication must be obtained and Form F completed before the procedure.
